A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q-Flow research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, Q-Flow benchmark evaluations, offline-to-online experiments, and ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results. Its use of previously published baseline scores does not negate the original Q-Flow experiments.

M1.justification: The flow-consistent intermediate value, gradient-matching policy objective, critic updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The ensemble-size reporting correction does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic distributions, standard and advanced OGBench tasks, and D4RL Antmaze tasks, including offline-to-online evaluation. Table 10(c)'s corrected setting label does not add task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, online experiments, and ablations. Section 5.2 newly explains why baseline sets differ between settings, but those sets already differed in v1.

E3.justification: Table 9(a) changes the reported standard-setting ensemble size from 10 to 2. This resolves a conflict with v1's Appendix C.3-C.4, which already specified 2; it establishes a setting-report correction without establishing that experiments were rerun. Other evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The policy-objective and guidance-source ablations, guidance-coefficient sensitivity, flow-step and time-embedding studies, gradient stability, value consistency, and training-cost analyses are retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 8 seeds for standard OGBench and 12 for advanced OGBench, with the same standard-deviation reporting. Figure 6 retains its 95% bootstrap confidence intervals; appendix uncertainty reporting is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Sections 5.3-5.4 correct reported gains from percent improvements to percentage-point differences. For example, unchanged scores of 54.4 versus 43.8 in Table 1 and 47.5 versus 44.8 in Table 2 support gaps of 10.6 and 2.7 points. This changes quantitative result reporting while preserving all underlying scores, curves, and rankings.

T1.justification: The hierarchical MDP definitions, deterministic-flow assumptions, flow-consistency identity in Equation (7), and subsequent mathematical objectives are unchanged. No derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: stable, expressive flow-policy optimization without BPTT and effective offline-to-online adaptation. The abstract already described the average advantage as 10.6 percentage points in v1.

C2.justification: The explanations of optimization stability and intermediate-value guidance remain unchanged. Both versions retain the complex-manipulation difficulties in Section 5.3 and the moving-target limitation in the conclusion and Appendix G.

D1.justification: Table 9(a) reconciles ensemble-size documentation with Appendix C, and Table 10(c) correctly identifies the advanced-setting guidance coefficients instead of labeling them standard-setting coefficients. Baseline-result provenance emphasized in v2's main text was already disclosed in v1's Appendix C.4.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research remain the same. Completing the missing Lyu et al. title and revising other bibliographic metadata do not introduce new references or research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized paragraph and terminology edits, brings existing baseline-source information into Section 5.2, adds acknowledgements, and updates publication and bibliography text. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 10(c)'s subcaption changes from standard to advanced setting. The proceedings footer and acknowledgements produce limited page and column reflow, while figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and internal consistency by correcting the ensemble-size discrepancy in Table 9(a) and the setting label in Table 10(c). The percentage-point corrections also make result reporting more precise. These are useful, limited improvements to documentation; the method and supporting empirical evidence remain unchanged.
